baseHeader.methodology: Source-linked original summaries and reference-guided educational reconstructions. Models and motion are unvalidated; artist titles do not independently verify taxonomy. Navigation groups are not a universal kingdom system. Microbial behavior depends on strain and conditions. Expansion entries are individually referenced authored morphology studies; legacy Protista/Monera reporting categories do not replace modern domains. Actual screenshots, software checks and draft status are distinct from independent scientific validation.

sources.title: Naturalis — Palaemon serratus diagnosis
sources.scope: Selected actual institutional diagnosis read for upcurved normally bifid rostrum, distal gap in dorsal dentition, two posterior dorsal teeth behind orbit, triramous antennules and pigment layout. Counts vary between taxonomic sources and are not a universal model-identification measurement.

sources.title: FAO Mediterranean identification guide — Palaemon serratus
sources.scope: Actual selected PDFpage12 printed239 diagnosis and whole-body, rostrum, P2-chela and antennular drawings viewed. Also selected family characters: two anterior chelate pairs and second pleuron overlapping first/third. Reported tooth-count ranges differ from Naturalis; selected tooth cues and proportions remain unmeasured. Historical fishery/range text is not current quantitative data.

retrieval.accessMethod: Selected actual PDF text and rendered figures

visual.fidelity: Original distinct reference reconstruction; fine anatomy, material optics and biological timing unmeasured
visual.description: Original laterally compressed carapace and continuous tapered six-somite abdomen replace the untextured repeated rounded segments. The selected upward-curved rostrum has posterior tooth cues, a distal dorsal gap and bifid-tip cue; second pleural plates overlap the adjacent regions. Two anterior small chelate pairs, with P2 larger than P1, precede three posterior main support pairs. Separate scaphocerites, three antennular flagellar cues, five simple pleopod pairs and a narrow telson with four uropodal lobes are retained. Original subdued grey-green cuticle, oblique cephalic and vertical abdominal brown bands and limited semitransparency. No source photograph pixels or measured tissue-optics calibration. The continuous cuticle deforms over the existing articulated joints; it does not exchange models between actions.
visual.scale: normalized display; not a specimen measurement

sources.title: Arnott, Neil & Ansell1998 — brown-shrimp tail-flip mechanism
sources.scope: Selected actual paper pages1–2/5–6 read and page6 Fig3/4 viewed. Escape involves anterior abdominal and cephalothorax flex, expanded scaphocerite head-fan and tail-fan, and often roll. This model offers only mild local flex, not that full measured escape mechanism; rates, coordinates, forces and trajectories are not imported.

retrieval.accessMethod: Selected actual primary PDF text and rendered figures

visual.fidelity: Original distinct reference reconstruction; fine anatomy, material optics and biological timing unmeasured
visual.description: Distinct flattened broad cephalothorax with a short unarmed rounded rostrum, continuous tapering abdomen, smooth sixth dorsal somite, stout first-pair subchelae and smaller second-pair chelae. Six posterior main walking limbs support the body. Separate antennal scales, five simple pleopod pairs, a telson and four uropodal lobes replace the same rounded draft used for the prawn. Original brown/cream fine mottling and darker fan ends replace a flat beige draft. The initial overly pale coarse speckling was reduced. Selected pigmentation is not a calibrated chromatophore state, scan, or photograph texture; fine dorsal segment boundaries and natural optical variation remain weak.
visual.scale: normalized display; not a specimen measurement
